source_paper.title: Heuristics in risky decision-making relate to preferential representation of information

evidence.locator: Results, Figs. 3–5; Methods: Participants, MEG analysis, Decoding outcome stimuli, Relating behavioral weighting of information to preferential representation of stimuli

evidence.locator: Fig. 3C,D and Methods: Decoding outcome stimuli

This is an original ordered accuracy endpoint, distinct from the descriptive reactivation/heuristic association.

cohort.description: Original N=19 main-analysis participants after excluding source IDs 6 and 19 from 21 recruits. split.description: The source primary relates within-participant choice-reactivation effects to between-participant behavioral weights; it is not held-out-participant prediction. Classifiers are fitted on localizer data and applied to choice events. Paper seven-fold held-out localizer validation is supporting, and its conflict with five-fold deposited code remains unresolved. Preserve original training/null examples, penalty selection and source participant-label permutation inference rather than introduce a new split.

inputs.description: Original localizer sensor epochs, seven stimulus classes and null examples support outcome classifiers. Choice-epoch continuous outcome activation probabilities, event probabilities/rewards, response times and choices must link to the original hierarchical EM probability/reward heuristic weights. Exact native artifact and identity bindings are unresolved. Accuracy labels alone are insufficient for the primary continuous-reactivation analysis.

preprocessing.description: Preserve source 0.5-Hz high-pass, 100-Hz downsampling, OSL sensor/ICA cleaning, absolute-95th-percentile scaling, lasso classifiers, probability-stimulus-locked choice epochs and response-time eligibility. Source joint first-level regressions, robust second-level fits and Gaussian sigma 1.5-bin smoothing define the original relation. Missing scaling helper, held-out scaling, differing temporal grids and probability-coefficient scaling remain unresolved; no silent repair establishes source parity.

metric.description: The primary outputs are both complete probability/reward prioritization maps and their associations with corresponding behavioral heuristic weights, including source robust-regression t-maps and 5000-draw maximum-statistic permutation inference. Four published peak t/pFWE summaries are partial visible source targets. No single favorable latency, decoder accuracy, stronger association or smaller p-value substitutes for the complete primary relationship or defines its improvement.

aggregation.description: Retain source trial-level outcome activation contrasts and joint probability/reward designs, yielding participant-specific first-level maps, followed by robust between-participant association with hierarchical behavioral weights across the original 19 people. Preserve unsmoothed/smoothed maps, original train/test support, maxima and all 5000 shuffled-participant maximum-statistic draws for each primary relationship. Trials, time cells and permutations are not independent participants. Exact map identities and observed-versus-null domain discrepancies remain unresolved.

full_panel.description:
Explicitly PARTIAL proposal: the four scalar findings are the published probability/reward peak t-statistics and corrected p-values for Figures 4–5. They do not represent the complete primary panel. Required native structured outputs remain unrepresented by scalar findings: (1) authentic N=19 participant/localizer/choice/behavior joins, event identities, original trial masks and response-time support; (2) source joint hierarchical EM behavioral probability/reward weights and fitting outputs needed to reproduce those estimates, without importing every unrelated alternative model; (3) continuous choice-reactivation outputs, joint trial designs, participant-specific probability/reward effects, both complete first-level and robust second-level train-by-test maps, unsmoothed/smoothed maps, peak coordinates and all 5000 participant-label maximum-null draws for each primary relationship; (4) supporting localizer class/null/penalty validation, activation and accuracy curves/maps, and transfer to choice presentations, with original folds, temporal support and cohort discrepancies unresolved; (5) source cross-axis specificity, unbiased/influence, response-alignment and relevant preprocessing/session-decoding controls. Preserve the safe-outcome single-participant-dependence caveat wherever that comparison supports interpretation. Exact source-native recipes and numerical references for these indispensable controls remain unresolved. No scalar average, invented category, placeholder vector or favorable selected latency replaces native maps.

Separate detection (Figure 6), neural BIS (Figure 7), detection-BIS non-replication, unrelated behavioral-model alternatives and sensor-topography exercises remain preserved as additional source evidence externally; they are not automatic primary completion requirements. There is no all-seven-figures or every-supplement obligation. Localizer decoding is supporting evidence, not a replacement primary. Numerical panel identities, computational verification and scientific agreement criteria must be frozen before admission.

permitted_observations.description: Matched primary reproduction conditions require the same authentic source paper, primary MEG/localizer/behavior data and observation protocol, with official author code as the only addition. Preserve source localizer-only classifier fitting, continuous choice reactivation with response-time censoring, hierarchical behavioral estimation and original participant-level inference. No authenticated common-input/exposure manifest, protected execution boundary or cumulative access/resource protocol is established. Visible source summaries cannot prove computation. The separate decoder-improvement proposal addresses a supporting result and cannot be forced into a same-target primary outcome bundle.

blocking_issues: The authorized primary is bounded Figures 4–5 neural–heuristic relationships with indispensable estimation/decoder controls. The unchanged improvement contract proposes secondary Figure 3 decoding. These are deliberately different scientific scopes; no same-target outcome bundle is admitted and no anchor equality is forced. Final task/binding integration remains pending.

Only four source-supported primary scalar summaries are declared. Both complete probability/reward maps, native intermediate outputs, all source maximum-null draws and indispensable companions remain unrepresented as findings and computationally unverified. Exact numerical panel membership, identities and independently justified agreement criteria remain unresolved; no convenient map scalarization is permitted.

Authenticate the original 19-person cohort (source IDs 6 and 19 excluded), event/sensor/localizer/choice/behavior identities, response-time masks and original joint hierarchical EM fit artifacts. Separate N=18 BIS and N=88 detection cohorts are not primary completion requirements.

Paper/code localizer validation disagrees on seven versus five folds, 19 versus 21 participants and temporal grids (paper test endpoint 800 ms; training script 850 ms; analysis 0:10:500 ms; epoch -250:10:600 ms). Original fold/seed identities and 50-versus-51 timepoint descriptions remain unresolved; supporting status does not waive these conflicts.

Deposited localizer code contains undefined pred_reg_epoch_im and absent scaleFunc and rescales held-out data by image class across test times. Original penalty choice uses the reported CV diagonal. Replacing source procedures or inventing independent evaluation would not establish historical parity.

The paper and deposited task-analysis code differ by a factor of two in the probability coefficient and in observed-versus-permutation map domains. Reconcile source conventions without silently normalizing or trimming the scientific target.

Indispensable specificity, unbiased/influence, response-alignment and preprocessing/session-decoding controls have article-described roles but incomplete source-native executable recipes and numerical references. Preserve the safe-association single-participant caveat wherever the safe comparison is interpreted; do not impose every unrelated supplement as primary.

The accepted localizer scorer performs supplied-logit arithmetic only; it is not a primary independent verifier. The prior localizer-to-task evaluator uses prospective scaling and participant-held-out behavioral prediction, not the original complete hierarchical estimation, robust maps and permutation inference. Authentic native input-dependent computation remains unproved.

Published scalar values are visible source inputs, not AI-computed results. No independently justified tolerance, numerical-variation criterion, authentic interface/output manifests or complete computational acceptance rule exists. Higher decoder accuracy, stronger association or smaller p-value does not define primary same-result improvement.

No authenticated matched paper+data versus paper+data+author-code protocol, exposure boundary, candidate freeze or cumulative access/resource budgets have been bound. Historical calibration and generated controls remain distinct from new scientific reproduction. Outcomes are not modified by this source-scope correction.
